newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine output up 8.5 pct in April - minister.
newsitem.headline: Argentine output up 8.5 pct in April - minister.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez on Wednesday said industrial output rose 8.5 percent in April and 7.0 percent for the first four months of the year compared with the corresponding periods of 1996.
He forecast Argentine consumer inflation would not exceed one percent this year. In 1996, consumer prices rose 0.05 percent increase.

"The industrial estimator for the first four months gives us growth of 7.0 percent and 8.5 percent in April," the minister said in a speech at Argentina's main annual banking conference. "Inflation will not exceed one percent in 1997."
Fernandez also forecast total bank loans to the "productive private sector" would reach $55 billion by the end of the year, after reaching almost $53 billion by the end of April.
The end-April level means loans rose 12 percent from a year earlier, he said.

The minister also revealed the total deposits in the banking system reached a record of $59 billion by the end of April -- "a sustained growth that shows economic operators have confidence in these policies we are applying with great determination."
